data.summary:
The r-3 QA-1 fix round is done: every assigned item plus rust-qa's QA-001 and QA-002 is addressed, and PR 26 CI is fully green on the fix-round head, including Windows. Pushed head is 7cfd413a73853d674ee43bd3c920113836f7dea0 on sprint/r-3-shared-http (PR 26 reports MERGEABLE). I merged origin/integrate/phase-a (r-3c, PR 25) at 6cad244 with a normal merge commit; a second fetch and merge before the final push found nothing new. Conflict resolution: clippy.toml keeps r-3c's allow-invalid = true together with r-3's single-read-site comment and reason; cargo-tree-gates.sh keeps r-3c's feature_rows and run_feature_row and adds r-3's rows under the new names graph_rows and run_graph_row. All rows pass.

Results by id:
- CI-R3-001 (f6bf365): the refused-connection test is renamed test_connect_phase_failure_is_retryable_and_not_retried. It now accepts Connect or Timeout and still asserts retryable and exactly one send. test (windows-2022) passes.
- REQ-QA-R3-001 (7cfd413): Implementation notes record your kit re-render in 8f969ff (pin 11b5b049, install.py --dry-run exit 0, sc-publish-dry-run.sh passed). Nothing under release/ changed after 8f969ff. The frontmatter 'open row' comment is gone; status stays in-review until QA-2.
- REQ-QA-R3-002: PR 26 checks are all green, run 42417451354 plus the dry-run check 42417451319, at 7cfd413. Not yet cited in the sprint doc, because the run finished after the doc commit (see follow-up).
- ARCH-R3-001 / REQ-QA-R3-003 (c85a8f6): an Active ADR-SAG-0007 r-3 bullet says timeouts are UreqTransport::new(Timeouts) construction state and with_timeouts is gone. The base sentence is marked superseded in part, and the sprint doc's ADR text item carries the same bullet verbatim.
- REQ-QA-R3-004 (c85a8f6): the a-10 ARCHC-018 row now reads 'superseded by r-3 (Timeouts on UreqTransport::new)'.
- RBQA-F101 (9b333dd, c85a8f6): the gate is now `rm -rf target/doc/sc_agent_http && cargo doc -p sc-agent-http && ! grep -rlE 'href="[^"]*ureq/|title="[a-z]+ ureq::' target/doc/sc_agent_http/`. The canary ran in a throwaway git worktree under scratchpad/r3-only/ with its own target dir. Each half on its own matched fn._canary.html (`<a class="struct" href="../ureq/agent/struct.Agent.html" title="struct ureq::agent::Agent">`) and the full gate exited 1; on the real tree it matches nothing. The step runs in the CI deps job (success), and plan.md and the r-3b doc carry the same command text.
- RBP-F007 (cc9c4cb, 93e53d5): sc-agent-http gains send_and_parse(transport, request, policy, cancel, parse) and HttpClient<T> (transport + BusyPolicy + CancelToken, with_busy_policy, with_cancel, send_and_parse). send_and_parse redacts the parse closure's error as well. JevClient and the Haiku/Luna client hold one HttpClient; the (HttpResponse, HttpRequest) tuple and every manual redact call are gone. Call sites add only the provider label, and the parse details no longer embed the name, so it appears once and final messages are unchanged. Facade and crate docs updated. The caller keeps the request, so a later r-6 send-site digest can read request.body() without changing the shape.
- RBQA-F102 (9b333dd): a CI grep in the deps job fails when disallowed_methods or ResolvedApiKey::as_str appears on a non-comment line outside ureq_transport.rs. Canary: an extra #[expect] in sc-jev makes it fail.
- RBQA-F103 (136f3d2): SecretHeader::matches exists only under test-util; manifest notes, rustdoc and crate docs say so.
- RBQA-F104 / RBQA-F009 (ebede9d, resolved in 6cad244): new tree-gate rows:
  - no ureq at depth 1 for sc-jev, sc-jev-backends and sc-jev-check;
  - sc-agent-http's forbidden packages, with a ureq positive control;
  - no workspace test-util in -e normal,features, with a dev-edge positive control;
  - sc-agent-http reaches sc-agent-types with feature secret only.
  Canaries: removing default-features = false fails the secret-only row, and a normal test-util edge from sc-jev fails the test-util row.
- FTQ-001 (39454b4): the stall test's request timeout is now 1 s, so the stall is the only possible cause.
- FTQ-002 (9b333dd): a CI step `cargo test -p sc-agent-http --features test-util` runs on all three OSes (success).
- Item 8 minors (cc9c4cb, 0b208fd):
  - provider endpoints are built once per Provider;
  - a request that cannot be built is now INPUT_INVALID (deterministic, not retryable);
  - an oversize response is RESPONSE_INVALID on both paths: ureq's BodyExceedsLimit is mapped there and the BodyTooLarge mapping is dropped;
  - test_util documents why it uses Arc<Mutex<_>>;
  - JevClientConfig accepts attempts 1..=4 and a timeout up to 120 s, with a bounds test;
  - retry docs state the double-charge rationale.
- QA-001 (93e53d5): new tests for sc-jev check.rs refusals, cancel-before-send and reply labels on both backends, backends validate.rs refusals, and sc-agent-http's &T/Arc<T> transport adapters, redact without a secret and the test doubles. The double 'Jev Jev' label in parse errors is fixed. Line coverage from `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --exclude sc-jev-py --all-features --summary-only` (before figures are rust-qa's):

| Scope | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workspace | 90.08 | 92.44 |
| sc-agent-http | 92.30 | 97.52 |
| sc-jev | 78.94 | 97.83 |
| sc-jev-backends | 87.76 | 95.56 |

  The 91.48 baseline is met.
- QA-002 (3c1c6a8): the kind stays Busy. BusyExhaustion::of(&JevError) returns Sends or Budget from the fixed detail endings this crate writes (SENDS_SUFFIX, BUDGET_SUFFIX); a backend's name prefix does not change the result. Asserted in test_exhaustion_reason_distinguishable; added to the facade.
- Item 9 (7cfd413): Implementation notes carry a per-id table with the requirement or ADR and commit for each item, and owned_paths lists the five parent-authorized paths.
- Reviewer canary check: `git diff crates/sc-agent-http/src/lib.rs` shows nothing, no `_canary` exists anywhere under crates/, and none of my uncommitted work was lost (my lib.rs changes were already committed in cc9c4cb).

Trailer: the first four fix-round commits (f6bf365, 39454b4, cc9c4cb, 136f3d2) carry the old 'Claude Fable 5.1' trailer because they were made before your trailer change; every commit from 0b208fd on uses 'Claude Opus 5.5'. I did not rewrite the pushed history.

`gh pr checks 26` at 7cfd413: all pass — coverage (llvm-cov), dependency gates (allocator, pins) including the new 'sc-agent-http public API has no ureq type', 'single ResolvedApiKey::as_str site' and 'cargo tree gates' steps, dry-run, python (macos-15, ubuntu-24.04, windows-2022), rustdoc (-D warnings), sc-treesitter feature matrix, and test (macos-15, ubuntu-24.04, windows-2022), each test job including the new sc-agent-http --features test-util step.
assumptions: For RBP-F007, every exchange error (transport, retry, non-200 or reply parse) gets the provider label at the call site. To keep final messages unchanged, the wire and check parse details dropped their own provider word. This is why parse_count and parse_vendor lost their provider argument.
BusyExhaustion::of reads detail endings that this crate alone writes. It is a typed accessor over a stable text contract, not a new error field, so it adds no new error id (planner resolution 5).
The ureq BodyExceedsLimit error is now mapped to RESPONSE_INVALID. NetworkErrorKind::BodyTooLarge is defined in sc-agent-types (r-1's crate) and was left untouched.
verification: Private gate script /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-randlee--claude-spares-spare-ZVG33J/84ad1f90-7f83-4b6e-b4fc-63121d353959/scratchpad/r3-only/validate.sh, log in validate.log: 47 of 48 lines PASS on the first run. The covered lines are cargo fetch --locked, fmt --check, just lint, just test, every named --exact test (each prints 1 passed), --test ureq, the widened public-API grep, the rg read-site, allow and lints checks, the sc-jev and sc-jev-backends suites, the errors golden test, the registry factory test, clippy (default and --all-features), the cargo tree checks, check-exact-pins, run-consumer-preflight, cargo test --workspace, sc-agent-http/sc-agent-types/sc-jev-check feature tests, rustdoc -D warnings, cargo hack for sc-treesitter and sc-agent-http, cargo-tree-gates.sh and just test-python.

The 48th line, the multi-crate cargo publish --dry-run --locked, failed locally with 'unresolved import sc_agent_http::HttpClient'. Cargo had reused a stale build of the unpublished sc-agent-http 0.1.0 from an earlier dry run. I deleted that run's extracted sc-agent-*/sc-jev* sources under ~/.cargo/registry/src/-5c9cccdfe1e33681/ and the worktree's target/package, but the stale build was still reused. Rerun with a fresh CARGO_TARGET_DIR it exits 0 and uploads all eight crates; PR 26's dry-run check is also green. This is recorded in the Implementation notes.
scripts/sc-publish-dry-run.sh was not re-run, because kit execution is not permitted in this session. Your 8f969ff run stands, and nothing under release/ or the kit workflows changed since.
gh pr checks 26 at 7cfd413: all green (run 42417451354; the dry-run check is run 42417451319).
follow_up: Sprint doc: add the PR 26 green-CI citation (run 42417451354 at 7cfd413) to the REQ-QA-R3-002 row. The run finished after the doc commit; I can push this in the next round, or you can add it with the QA-2 dispatch.
QA-2 on 7cfd413; status stays in-review until it passes.
r-3b: keep the widened public-API gate and the graph_rows in place, and add the sc-agent-compose forbidden edge once that crate exists.

Local only: target/ in this worktree still holds a stale package build of the unpublished sc-agent-http 0.1.0, so a local multi-crate publish dry-run there needs a fresh CARGO_TARGET_DIR (or a cargo clean). CI is unaffected.
